quotation.text: Differentiating the twisted exact equation gives v'=B(v,v)/2.

background_notes.fact: For A>0 and r>0, Fourier projections contract every H^s norm, ||P_(>A)u||_(H^(-r))<=A^(-r)||u||_2 and ||P_(>A)u||_2<=A^(-1)||u||_(H^1). For N>=2, ||P_(<=N) partial_x^2 u||_2<=N^2||u||_2. These projections commute with the multipliers S_t, Dinv and spatial derivatives.

grounds.reason: Sobolev norms are weighted Fourier square sums and projections retain the stated frequencies.
S_t is a scalar multiplier at each frequency.
Spatial derivatives and Dinv are scalar Fourier multipliers.
The threshold is an arbitrary real N>=2; the bounds are applied to smooth periodic paths and J outputs in H^1.

background_notes.justification: Deleting summands contracts the nonnegative weighted square sums. On |k|>A, <k>^(-r)<=A^(-r) and <k>^(-1)<=A^(-1); on |k|<=N, |k|^2<=N^2. Squaring these pointwise inequalities and summing gives the bounds. Diagonal multipliers commute. Consequently N005's Dinv P(FG) estimate yields the stated N^2 low-frequency bound, since partial_x(FG)=partial_x^2 Dinv P(FG).

background_notes.fact: The trilinear operator Cint has output frequency k=k1+k2+k3. Thus P_(>N)Cint(P_(<=N/3)f1,P_(<=N/3)f2,P_(<=N/3)f3)=0. Fixed spatial projections commute with weak time differentiation and contract X on every subinterval.

grounds.reason: Cint is formed from two spatial products and Fourier multipliers.
The projections retain the specified Fourier frequencies.
X uses an L2 supremum and a negative Sobolev weak derivative supremum.
N006 supplies Cint on paths with the required finite X norms.
The proof explicitly decomposes all three inputs at N/3.

background_notes.justification: Each retained input frequency has modulus <=N/3, so each resulting product frequency has modulus <=N by the triangle inequality; S, P and Dinv never change a frequency. The low-frequency projected inputs have finite Fourier support, so this support assertion needs no interchange of infinite products or integrals. Multilinearity gives the three remaining terms exactly as displayed. Bounded fixed linear projections commute with distributional time differentiation by testing the weak derivative identity, and contraction follows from the Fourier norm sums. Restriction to a shorter interval cannot increase either supremum.
